title: Issue tokens that nobody can mistake for cards or trace back to them

cases.says: a card gets a 16-digit token, the same requestor gets the same token again, another card gets another, and each token leads back to its card
every token ends with the Luhn check digit of its first fifteen digits, so checks built for card numbers accept it
every token starts with the range reserved for tokens, so it can never be a real card number
the same card presented by two requestors gets two different tokens
apart from the range and the check digit, a token's digits are drawn at random; none are copied from the card
a new draw that equals an issued token is drawn again, so the issued token keeps leading to its own card
nothing the vault keeps holds a clear card number: it files tokens under the keyed lookup value

origin.section: 14.4. A Token Belongs to the Requestor It Was Issued To
